name: Arcadia Planitia
coordinate_note: Per-site numbers were collected by Hermes with source URLs and not independently re-checked by Claude. status=sourced means a URL exists; unverified means no published number was found (leave empty, do not estimate); weak_source means the only source is Wikipedia and should be replaced. Site coordinates are approximate and from memory: verify against the USGS Mars gazetteer before use.

verified.detail: Cited doi page blocked; confirmed via Bramson EPSC2017-425 abstract: 30-80 m across Arcadia (Bramson+ 2015 GRL 42).
Bramson+ 2015 GRL abstract (record): excess water ice ~10^4 km3.

LPSC 2018 #2606 says '35 +/- 15 wt% ice below the surface' (GRS, via Boynton 2002 / Pathare 2017); it does not use the term water-equivalent hydrogen. Key renamed. Our own neutron flux there is low (4.19 counts/s, 20th percentile), consistent with hydrogen-rich ground.
LPSC 2018 #2606: sinuous (ice) units 200-250; surroundings 100-200. Our THEMIS sample at 44N 202.5E reads 297 (277-315): different place and method, not a contradiction.

facts.value: optically thick dust over most of the region (TES dust cover index)

verified.detail: LPSC 2018 #2606: optically thick dust overlies most of Arcadia (Ruff & Christensen 2002).

The cited LPSC abstract does not mention basaltic lavas, cinder cones or mantle; it describes a dusty, flat plain with sand-dominated soil, polygonal terrain, few rocks >1 m. Claim removed until a source is found.

facts.unit: m (MOLA, 5th-95th percentile within 300 km of the site point)

verified.detail: Wikipedia says 0 to -3 km for the plain (centre 47.2N 184.3E). MOLA at this site point (44N 202.5E) is -3,918 m; median within 300 km is -3,928 m (p5-p95 -3,984 to -3,859). Replaced with MOLA.

The ~140 Myr median is from a study of pedestal craters in both hemispheres (Planetary and Space Science 2014), not Arcadia alone. Key renamed; do not present as an Arcadia age. Publisher page blocked, figure confirmed from the paper's abstract record.
